topic.label: Space Simulation Engineering
topic.desc: Engineering on-demand space simulations with SCWs and agents: scale worlds, catalog substrate, on-demand generation, agent triggers, sky experiments and verification. Built as the physical-space counterpart of Maxey0 latent space engineering.

concepts: Each simulation scale is a Structured Context World: solar system in AU, Local Bubble in light years, Milky Way in kiloparsecs, with typed relations between parent and child worlds. Mirrors latent world construction in Maxey0.

The measured data every scale stands on: star, exoplanet, cluster, pulsar and orbit catalogs with provenance, units and epochs. Mirrors latent space engineering: the substrate all measurement depends on.
Objects created when a user action asks for them, not stored permanently: densified regions, galaxy particle models, exoplanet orbits. Generated objects are labeled and deterministic per seed.

In-app events (select a star, open a menu, set a date) mapped to actions: a direct tool call or a structured message that hands the job to an agent. The trigger table is data, so new triggers need no code.

Scientific and historical experiments run inside the simulation: whether a comet was visible on a past date, what crossed a region of sky, how a galaxy would look from here. Calendar conventions and model limits are part of the answer.
Independent checking of every generated or computed result: physics evals, unit and frame checks, catalog-versus-generated labels and CPU budgets for hosted tools.
skills: Hand a view from one scale world to the next (Oort Cloud to Local Bubble, 15,000 ly to the galaxy) keeping frames and units consistent.
Type the relation between a child world and its parent: contains, superposes, passes-through or signals.
Bring a catalog extract (stars, exoplanets, clusters, pulsars) into a scale with its source, epoch and units recorded.
Mark every value as catalog data, model output or generated, and carry the source with it.
Fill a region with stars at the local stellar density and spectral mix, seeded and labeled as generated.
Place a particle model of a named galaxy at its measured position, distance and orientation.
Add a star's confirmed planets from the archive when the star is selected, with orbits drawn to a stated enlargement.
Define app events and the actions they fire: automatic direct tool calls, buttons, or agent messages.
Route a trigger message to the right agent with a prompt hook and return the agent's summary to the conversation.
Compute distance, elongation and apparent magnitude of a small body on a past date with the correct calendar and era convention.
Turn a question about the sky into runs over candidate bodies and dates, including both readings of an ambiguous year.
Run the physics and structure evals for a world and everything below it, and report passed over total.
Measure each hosted tool against the per-request CPU limit and assign it to the free or paid tier.
mcp: Space-at-Scale MCP server: three-scale space simulation with SCW graph, mining, trips, galaxy field, and agent builders (exoplanet systems, region densify, galaxy build, sky check).

provenance.mcp_notes: Only the Space-at-Scale server is listed: its repository was opened and its tools exercised this session. No other astronomy MCP server was verified, so none is listed.
